name: Push-up
instructions: Set your hands slightly wider than shoulder width, fingers spread, and step your feet back so your body forms a straight line.
Brace your core and glutes, then lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows to about 45 degrees from your torso.
Stop when your chest is a fist's height from the floor, then press the floor away until your elbows are straight.
cues: Keep a straight line from ears to heels; do not let the hips sag.
Screw your hands into the floor to keep the shoulders stable.
Lower for about two seconds and press up with control.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees, which stresses the front of the shoulder.
Letting the lower back arch or the hips drop as you tire.
Bouncing out of the bottom instead of controlling the descent.

name: Incline push-up
instructions: Place your hands on a bench or sturdy surface slightly wider than shoulder width.
Walk your feet back until your body is straight and your chest is over your hands.
Lower your chest to the bench, then press back up without losing your body line.
cues: The higher the surface, the easier the rep; start higher than you think you need.
Keep ribs down and glutes tight.
Push the bench away rather than thinking about lifting your body.
mistakes: Choosing a surface so low that the hips sag.
Leaning the head forward before the chest moves.
Rushing the descent.

name: Dumbbell bench press
instructions: Sit on the bench with dumbbells resting on your thighs, then lie back and bring them to chest level.
Set your shoulder blades back and down, feet flat, and press the dumbbells up until the arms are straight.
Lower with control until the elbows are just below the bench line, then press again.
cues: Keep wrists stacked over elbows.
Use a slight arc rather than a perfectly straight bar path.
Leave a small gap between the dumbbells at the top to keep tension.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
Bouncing the dumbbells off the chest.
Lifting the hips off the bench to press.

name: Incline dumbbell press
instructions: Set a bench to roughly 20–30 degrees and sit back with dumbbells at chest height.
Press the weights up and slightly together until the arms are straight.
Lower under control until you feel a stretch across the upper chest.
cues: Keep the bench angle modest; steep angles shift work to the shoulders.
Keep the shoulder blades pinned to the bench.
Stop the set if the front of the shoulder pinches.
mistakes: Setting the bench too steep and turning it into a shoulder press.
Letting the dumbbells drift too far back behind the body.
Using momentum from the hips.

name: Cable chest fly
instructions: Set the pulleys around chest height and step forward with one foot, holding a handle in each hand.
With a soft bend in the elbows, sweep the hands together in front of your chest.
Squeeze briefly, then let the arms open until you feel a gentle stretch.
cues: Keep the elbow angle fixed; the movement happens at the shoulder.
Move slowly and stay within a comfortable range.
Keep the ribs stacked over the pelvis.
mistakes: Turning the fly into a press by bending and straightening the elbows.
Opening the arms too far behind the body.
Leaning back and using body weight to move the stack.

name: Machine chest press
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles sit around mid-chest height.
Press the handles forward until the arms are almost straight, keeping your back against the pad.
Return slowly until the hands are level with the chest.
cues: Keep your wrists neutral and elbows slightly tucked.
Let the chest stretch at the end of the return, but do not force it.
Use a controlled tempo of about two seconds down.
mistakes: Setting the seat too high and pressing above the chest.
Slamming the weight stack.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.

name: Pull-up
instructions: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Start the pull by drawing the shoulder blades down, then drive the elbows toward your ribs.
Lower with control until the arms are straight.
cues: Think chest to bar rather than chin to bar.
Keep the legs together and avoid swinging.
Use a band or machine assistance if you cannot control the descent.
mistakes: Kipping or swinging to get the chin over the bar.
Shrugging at the bottom and starting with bent arms.
Dropping quickly from the top instead of lowering with control.

name: Lat pulldown
instructions: Set the thigh pad snug and grip the bar a little wider than shoulder width.
Sit tall, draw the shoulder blades down, and pull the bar toward the upper chest.
Let the bar rise slowly until the arms are straight and the lats stretch.
cues: Keep the torso nearly upright, with a slight lean back.
Pull with the elbows, not the hands.
Control the return for three seconds.
mistakes: Pulling the bar behind the neck.
Leaning far back and using body weight.
Letting the shoulders rise toward the ears at the start.

name: Seated cable row
instructions: Sit with the feet braced and grab the handle with straight arms.
Pull the handle toward your lower ribs while keeping the torso still.
Squeeze the shoulder blades, then return slowly until the arms are straight.
cues: Keep the chest tall and the spine neutral.
Let the shoulder blades move; do not lock them in place.
Do not rock back and forth for momentum.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back as the handle returns.
Shrugging the shoulders during the pull.
Using a jerking motion with the torso.

name: Single-arm dumbbell row
instructions: Place one hand and knee on a bench, with the other foot on the floor and a dumbbell in the free hand.
Let the dumbbell hang, then row it toward your hip by driving the elbow back.
Lower slowly to a full stretch and complete the reps before switching sides.
cues: Keep the hips square to the floor.
Think of putting the dumbbell in your back pocket.
Do not rotate the torso to lift the weight.
mistakes: Twisting the torso to gain leverage.
Shrugging the working shoulder.
Cutting the stretch short at the bottom.

name: Inverted row
instructions: Set a bar at waist height, lie under it, and grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Keep a straight line from head to heels and pull your chest toward the bar.
Lower with control until the arms are straight.
cues: Start with the body more upright to make it easier.
Squeeze the glutes to keep the hips from sagging.
Pull the elbows down and back, not out.
mistakes: Letting the hips drop and arching the lower back.
Pulling the chin forward instead of moving the chest.
Bouncing at the bottom.

name: Face pull
instructions: Set a rope at upper chest or eye height and hold one end in each hand.
Pull the rope toward your forehead, spreading the hands apart.
Squeeze the rear shoulders, then return slowly with control.
cues: Keep the elbows high and wide.
Use light weight and focus on the squeeze.
Stand tall without leaning back.
mistakes: Using too much weight and turning it into a row.
Pulling the rope down toward the chest instead of the face.
Shrugging the shoulders.

name: Dumbbell overhead press
instructions: Stand tall with dumbbells at shoulder height and palms facing forward.
Brace your core and press the weights overhead until the arms are straight.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height.
cues: Keep the ribs down and glutes tight to avoid arching.
Press slightly back and up so the weights finish over the ears.
Use a grip just outside shoulder width.
mistakes: Leaning back and turning it into an incline press.
Pressing the weights forward of the body.
Flaring the wrists back.

name: Machine shoulder press
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles start around shoulder height.
Press the handles overhead until the arms are almost straight.
Lower slowly to the starting position.
cues: Keep your back against the pad.
Stop just short of locking out to keep tension.
Let the shoulders stay down away from the ears.
mistakes: Setting the seat too low.
Arching the back off the pad.
Letting the weight drop quickly.

name: Dumbbell lateral raise
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at your sides and a slight bend in the elbows.
Raise the arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lower slowly with control.
cues: Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
Keep the shoulders relaxed and down.
Use light weights and stop at shoulder height.
mistakes: Swinging the weights up with momentum.
Raising above shoulder height and shrugging.
Leaning the torso back.

name: Rear delt fly
instructions: Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back and dumbbells hanging below the shoulders.
With a soft elbow bend, raise the arms out to the sides until level with the torso.
Squeeze the rear shoulders, then lower slowly.
cues: Keep the neck in line with the spine.
Think of reaching the arms long rather than lifting high.
Use a light weight and a slow tempo.
mistakes: Rounding the back during the hinge.
Using momentum from the torso.
Shrugging the shoulders as the arms rise.

name: Pike push-up
instructions: Start in a push-up position, then walk your feet toward your hands and lift the hips high.
Bend the elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor in front of your hands.
Press back up until the arms are straight.
cues: Keep the hips high throughout.
Look at your feet or the floor just behind your hands.
Elevate your feet on a step to make it harder.
mistakes: Lowering the hips and turning it into a regular push-up.
Letting the elbows flare wide.
Dropping the head too quickly.

name: Bodyweight squat
instructions: Stand with feet about shoulder width apart and toes slightly turned out.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower as far as you can control.
Drive through the whole foot to stand back up.
cues: Keep the knees tracking in line with the toes.
Reach the hips back before the knees bend.
Keep the chest tall and heels grounded.
mistakes: Letting the knees cave inward.
Rising onto the toes.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom.

name: Goblet squat
instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height with both hands.
Sit the hips down and back, keeping the weight close to the chest.
Descend as far as is comfortable, then drive through the feet to stand.
cues: Use the weight as a counterbalance to stay tall.
Keep the elbows inside the knees at the bottom.
Pause for a moment at the bottom if you can control it.
mistakes: Letting the weight pull you forward.
Knees collapsing inward.
Losing tension at the bottom.

name: Barbell back squat
instructions: Set the bar on your upper back, brace your core, and stand with feet shoulder width apart.
Break at the hips and knees to lower under control, keeping the chest proud.
Drive up through the whole foot to return to standing.
cues: Brace as if bracing for a light punch.
Keep the bar over the middle of the foot.
Use spotters or a rack with safety bars when training heavy.
mistakes: Letting the knees cave in.
Good-morning the weight by folding the chest forward.
Adding load before the movement pattern is solid.

name: Leg press
instructions: Sit with your back and hips against the pad and feet shoulder width apart on the platform.
Lower the platform until the knees are bent to a comfortable depth.
Press back up without locking the knees hard.
cues: Keep the lower back against the pad.
Keep the knees tracking over the toes.
Leave a small bend at the top.
mistakes: Going so deep that the hips lift off the pad.
Locking the knees aggressively.
Placing the feet too low on the platform.

name: Split squat
instructions: Step one foot forward into a long stance and keep the torso tall.
Lower straight down until the front knee is around 90 degrees.
Push through the front foot to return to the top.
cues: Think down and up, not forward.
Keep most of the weight through the front foot.
Hold a rail for balance while learning.
mistakes: Letting the front knee cave inward.
Bouncing at the bottom.
Taking a stance so short the heel lifts.

name: Walking lunge
instructions: From standing, step forward and lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees.
Push through the front foot to bring the back foot forward into the next lunge.
Continue alternating legs with control.
cues: Keep the torso tall and eyes forward.
Aim for a soft landing with each step.
Use a shorter step if balance is limited.
mistakes: Crashing the back knee into the floor.
Lunging with a stance that is too narrow.
Letting the front knee collapse inward.

name: Step-up
instructions: Face a bench or step at about knee height and place one whole foot on it.
Drive through that foot to stand on the step without pushing off the back leg.
Lower slowly and repeat on the same side before switching.
cues: Keep the knee aligned with the middle toes.
Control the descent rather than dropping.
Start with a lower step if you feel unstable.
mistakes: Pushing off the floor with the back foot.
Letting the standing knee cave inward.
Using a step so high the hips shift sideways.

name: Wall sit
instructions: Lean your back against a wall and walk your feet out until the knees are around 90 degrees.
Keep the back flat against the wall and hold the position.
Stand up before your form breaks.
cues: Keep the knees over the ankles.
Breathe normally rather than holding your breath.
Choose a depth you can hold with good form.
mistakes: Letting the knees travel far past the toes.
Sliding down until the hips are below the knees.
Holding your breath.

name: Romanian deadlift
instructions: Start standing with the weights at your thighs and a soft bend in the knees.
Push the hips back and let the weights slide down the legs while keeping the back flat.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then drive the hips forward to stand.
cues: Think of closing a car door with your hips.
Keep the weights close to the legs.
Keep the neck in line with the spine.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to go deeper.
Squatting the weight instead of hinging.
Letting the weights drift away from the body.

name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in one hand and shift your weight onto the opposite leg.
Hinge at the hip and let the free leg extend behind you as the chest lowers.
Return to standing by driving the hips forward, then switch sides.
cues: Keep the hips square to the floor.
Reach the free heel toward the wall behind you.
Use a light weight until balance is reliable.
mistakes: Letting the hips rotate open.
Rounding the back at the bottom.
Trying to touch the floor instead of stopping at control.

name: Glute bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip width apart.
Press through the heels to lift the hips until your body forms a straight line.
Squeeze the glutes at the top, then lower slowly.
cues: Tuck the ribs down and avoid arching the lower back.
Push the heels into the floor rather than the toes.
Pause for one second at the top.
mistakes: Overextending the lower back at the top.
Letting the knees splay out.
Rushing the reps.

name: Hip thrust
instructions: Rest your upper back on a bench and place the weight across your hips.
Plant the feet and drive the hips up until the torso is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze, then lower with control.
cues: Keep the chin slightly tucked.
Use a pad across the hips for comfort.
Keep the ribs down rather than arching.
mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back.
Letting the knees cave inward.
Placing the feet too far away or too close.

name: Machine hamstring curl
instructions: Adjust the pad just above the heels and lie face down with hips flat.
Curl the heels toward the glutes without lifting the hips.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
cues: Keep the hips pressed into the pad.
Squeeze the hamstrings at the top.
Control the lowering phase.
mistakes: Lifting the hips to help the weight.
Swinging the weight up.
Cutting the return short.

name: Kettlebell swing
instructions: Stand with feet just wider than the hips and hold the kettlebell in front of you.
Hinge at the hips to swing the bell back between the legs, then snap the hips forward.
Let the bell float to chest height and guide it back into the next hinge.
cues: The power comes from the hips, not the arms.
Keep the core braced and the back flat.
Finish tall with glutes squeezed.
mistakes: Squatting the bell up instead of hinging.
Rounding the back during the backswing.
Lifting the bell with the shoulders.

name: Standing calf raise
instructions: Stand tall with the balls of your feet on a step and heels hanging off.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can, pause briefly.
Lower slowly until you feel a stretch in the calves.
cues: Keep the knees almost straight.
Use a wall for balance if needed.
Move slowly through the full range.
mistakes: Bouncing quickly through tiny reps.
Bending the knees to help.
Cutting off the stretch at the bottom.

name: Single-leg calf raise
instructions: Stand on one foot with the ball of the foot on a step.
Rise onto the toes as high as possible, keeping the ankle stable.
Lower slowly and switch sides after the set.
cues: Hold a wall or rail for balance.
Keep the ankle moving straight up and down.
Use a full range of motion.
mistakes: Rolling the ankle outward or inward.
Going too fast and using momentum.
Letting the heel slam down.

name: Forearm plank
instructions: Set the elbows under the shoulders and extend the legs behind you.
Squeeze the glutes and brace the core so the body forms a straight line.
Hold while breathing steadily, then stop when form breaks.
cues: Push the forearms into the floor.
Tuck the ribs down slightly.
Stop the set rather than letting the hips sag.
mistakes: Holding the breath.
Letting the hips sag or pike up.
Chasing time with poor form.

name: Side plank
instructions: Lie on one side with the elbow under the shoulder and legs stacked.
Lift the hips so the body forms a straight line.
Hold, then lower and switch sides.
cues: Keep the hips stacked, not rolled forward.
Bend the knees to make it easier.
Keep the ear away from the shoulder.
mistakes: Rolling the top hip back.
Sinking into the bottom shoulder.
Holding your breath.

name: Dead bug
instructions: Lie on your back with arms up and knees bent to 90 degrees over the hips.
Press the lower back gently into the floor and extend one arm and the opposite leg.
Return and repeat on the other side.
cues: Move slowly and keep the lower back connected to the floor.
Exhale as you extend.
Reduce the range if the back lifts.
mistakes: Letting the lower back arch.
Moving too fast.
Holding your breath.

name: Hollow body hold
instructions: Lie on your back and press the lower back into the floor.
Lift the shoulder blades and legs slightly off the floor with arms overhead.
Hold with control, then relax.
cues: Keep the lower back flat; bend the knees to scale down.
Reach the arms past the ears.
Breathe shallow but steady.
mistakes: Letting the back arch off the floor.
Holding the neck and straining it.
Chasing a long hold with bad positioning.

name: Hanging knee raise
instructions: Hang from a bar with straight arms and shoulders gently engaged.
Curl the knees up toward the chest without swinging.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
cues: Start with the pelvis tucked.
Use a controlled tempo; stop if you start swinging.
Let go and reset between reps if needed.
mistakes: Swinging to create momentum.
Only lifting the legs with the hip flexors and not the abs.
Dropping out of the hold.

name: Pallof press
instructions: Stand sideways to the cable or band anchor with the handle at chest height.
Press the handle straight out from the chest while resisting rotation.
Return slowly and repeat, then switch sides.
cues: Keep the hips square to the front.
Press out until the arms are straight.
Use a weight light enough that the torso stays still.
mistakes: Twisting toward the anchor.
Shrugging the shoulder.
Using too much weight and losing the anti-rotation benefit.

name: Dumbbell curl
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at your sides and palms facing forward.
Curl the weights toward the shoulders with the elbows staying near the ribs.
Lower slowly to the start.
cues: Keep the wrists neutral.
Do not swing the torso.
Control the lowering phase.
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight.
Letting the elbows drift forward.
Dropping the weights quickly.

name: Hammer curl
instructions: Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other at your sides.
Curl the weights up while keeping the palms facing inward.
Lower slowly to the start.
cues: Keep the elbows close to the body.
Squeeze at the top without leaning back.
Use a full, controlled range.
mistakes: Rocking the torso.
Letting the elbows move forward.
Half reps at the bottom.

name: Resistance band curl
instructions: Stand on the middle of a band and hold the ends with palms facing up.
Curl the handles toward your shoulders against the band tension.
Lower slowly and keep tension.
cues: Keep the elbows pinned to your sides.
Stand tall without leaning back.
Adjust your stance to change resistance.
mistakes: Leaning back to fight the band.
Letting the band snap back.
Elbows drifting forward.

name: Triceps pushdown
instructions: Stand at a high pulley with a rope or bar and elbows at your sides.
Push the handle down until the arms are straight.
Let the handle rise slowly until the elbows are around 90 degrees.
cues: Keep the elbows fixed beside the ribs.
Squeeze the triceps at the bottom.
Keep the shoulders relaxed.
mistakes: Elbows flaring out or drifting forward.
Leaning over the weight.
Using the shoulders to press down.

name: Overhead triceps extension
instructions: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands.
Bend the elbows to lower the weight behind your head.
Straighten the arms to return to the top.
cues: Keep the elbows pointing forward.
Keep the ribs down and core braced.
Use a weight you can control behind the head.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows wide.
Arching the lower back.
Moving too fast into the bottom position.

name: Close-grip push-up
instructions: Set your hands just inside shoulder width and form a straight plank.
Lower your chest with the elbows close to the ribs.
Press up until the arms are straight.
cues: Keep the elbows tucked at about 30 degrees.
Keep the body in one line.
Do the reps on an incline if the full version is too hard.
mistakes: Placing the hands together and stressing the wrists.
Flaring the elbows.
Letting the hips sag.

name: Mountain climber
instructions: Start in a high plank with hands under the shoulders.
Drive one knee toward the chest and switch legs with control.
Continue alternating at a steady pace.
cues: Keep the hips low and the shoulders over the hands.
Start slow before adding pace.
Keep the core braced so the back does not bounce.
mistakes: Letting the hips pike up.
Bouncing the lower back.
Letting the shoulders drift past the hands.

name: Farmer carry
instructions: Hold a heavy weight in each hand at your sides.
Walk with short, steady steps while keeping the torso tall.
Set the weights down with a hinge, not a rounded back.
cues: Keep the shoulders down and back.
Brace the core and breathe.
Take short steps to stay stable.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders.
Leaning to one side.
Dropping the weights with a rounded back.

name: Rowing machine intervals
instructions: Strap in with the damper set around 4–6 and sit tall.
Drive with the legs first, then swing the torso and pull the handle to the lower ribs.
Reverse the order to return: arms, torso, legs.
cues: Think legs, body, arms on the drive.
Keep the chain moving level.
Use a pace you can repeat rather than sprinting the first minute.
mistakes: Pulling with the arms before the legs.
Rounding the back at the catch.
Setting the damper to 10 for every session.

name: Incline walk
instructions: Set the treadmill to a comfortable walking pace.
Raise the incline gradually to a level you can sustain while breathing steadily.
Walk for the planned duration, then lower the incline and cool down.
cues: Stay tall rather than holding the rails.
Aim to breathe a little harder than at rest but still hold a conversation.
Increase incline before speed if you have joint concerns.
mistakes: Holding the handrails and leaning back.
Starting at a steep incline and burning out.
Skipping the cool-down.

name: Bike intervals
instructions: Set the seat so the knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Warm up for a few minutes, then alternate a harder effort with an easy recovery.
Cool down with easy spinning.
cues: Keep the cadence smooth rather than grinding.
The hard effort should feel strong but controlled.
End the session feeling like you could do one more interval.
mistakes: Starting intervals without a warm-up.
Setting the resistance so high the knees ache.
Skipping recovery between efforts.

name: Jump rope
instructions: Hold the handles at hip height and start with small, quick wrist turns.
Jump just an inch or two off the floor, landing softly.
Keep the pace steady for the planned time.
cues: Turn the rope with the wrists, not the arms.
Land quietly through the balls of the feet.
Take breaks before form breaks.
mistakes: Jumping too high.
Landing heavily on the heels.
Swinging the arms instead of the wrists.

name: Burpee
instructions: From standing, squat down and place your hands on the floor.
Step or jump your feet back into a plank, then bring them forward again.
Stand up and finish with a small hop or a tall stand.
cues: Step the feet back instead of jumping to reduce impact.
Keep the core braced in the plank position.
Scale the pace rather than sacrificing form.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag in the plank.
Landing hard on the knees.
Sprinting through reps until form collapses.

name: Cat-cow
instructions: Start on all fours with hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips.
Inhale and drop the belly, lifting the chest and tailbone into cow.
Exhale and round the spine, tucking the chin and pelvis into cat.
cues: Move slowly with the breath.
Spread the fingers and keep the wrists comfortable.
Make the movement feel good rather than forcing range.
mistakes: Rushing the movement.
Letting the shoulders shrug toward the ears.
Forcing the neck into a painful range.

name: World's greatest stretch
instructions: Step into a long lunge and place both hands inside the front foot.
Drop the back knee if comfortable, then rotate the front arm toward the ceiling.
Return the hand, shift back, and repeat before switching sides.
cues: Move slowly and breathe into each position.
Keep the front knee aligned with the toes.
Do not force the rotation.
mistakes: Rushing through the positions.
Letting the front knee cave inward.
Holding your breath.

name: Kneeling hip flexor stretch
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the other foot in front, forming two 90-degree angles.
Tuck the pelvis under and gently shift the hips forward.
Hold while breathing, then switch sides.
cues: Tuck the tailbone before leaning forward.
Keep the ribs down.
Use a cushion under the knee if needed.
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of tucking the pelvis.
Leaning so far that the front knee hurts.
Bouncing in the stretch.

name: Open book thoracic rotation
instructions: Lie on your side with knees bent to 90 degrees and arms stacked in front.
Keep the knees together and sweep the top arm across your body toward the floor behind you.
Return slowly and repeat, then switch sides.
cues: Follow your hand with your eyes.
Keep the knees stacked and still.
Exhale as you open.
mistakes: Letting the knees roll apart.
Forcing the shoulder to the floor.
Moving quickly.

name: Seated hamstring stretch
instructions: Sit with one leg extended and the other bent with the foot toward the inner thigh.
Hinge forward from the hip over the extended leg until you feel a gentle stretch.
Hold, breathe, and switch sides.
cues: Keep the back long rather than rounding.
Stretch to a gentle tension, not pain.
Relax the shoulders.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach the toes.
Bouncing.
Pushing into sharp pain.

name: Child's pose
instructions: Start on all fours, then sit the hips back toward the heels.
Reach the arms forward and rest the forehead on the floor or a cushion.
Breathe slowly and relax into the position.
cues: Widen the knees if the hips feel tight.
Let the shoulders soften.
Stay only as long as it feels comfortable.
mistakes: Forcing the hips down.
Holding tension in the shoulders.
Continuing if it causes knee or back pain.

name: Band shoulder pass-through
instructions: Hold a light band with a wide grip in front of your hips.
Keeping the arms straight, bring the band up and over your head to your lower back.
Reverse the path slowly with control.
cues: Use a wider grip if the shoulders feel pinched.
Keep the ribs down and core braced.
Move slowly and stay below pain.
mistakes: Using a grip that is too narrow.
Arching the back to get the band over.
Rushing the movement.

name: Knee-to-wall ankle mobility
instructions: Stand facing a wall with one foot a few inches back and the heel planted.
Drive the front knee toward the wall over the middle toes.
Return and repeat, then switch sides.
cues: Keep the heel down throughout.
Aim the knee over the second toe.
Move slowly into the end range.
mistakes: Letting the heel lift.
Rolling the ankle outward.
Bouncing at the end range.
